numinance.kinds.v1.Metadata.jsonschema.s.description: Metadata names a kind object and fixes its scope.

name.description: name is required and unique per kind and scope; other kinds reference the object by it.

scope.description: scope is required and not SCOPE_UNSPECIFIED; the loader enforces the latter.
scope.title: Scope

numinance.kinds.v1.Metadata.jsonschema.s.title: Metadata

numinance.kinds.v1.ResidencyFloors.jsons.description: ResidencyFloors is the set of floors; it is one message so the whole set carries the FORBID directive.

floor.description: floor is required: it applies to every change, together with every matching rule's floor.
floor.title: Residency Class

rules.description: rules add floors per component and environment; a rule never relaxes floor.

numinance.kinds.v1.ResidencyFloors.jsons.title: Residency Floors

numinance.kinds.v1.ResidencyMatch.jsonsc.description:
ResidencyMatch selects changes; an absent key matches every value and an empty match matches every change, and a
 key the change has no value for counts as a match. Floors from the org and control packs all hold together.

component.description:
component is the name of the component the change touches. It is not a security boundary until floors match only
 components of an org-owned SIGNED_POLICY registry, since a repo can rename one.

environment.description: environment is the name of the environment the change acts in.

numinance.kinds.v1.ResidencyMatch.jsonsc.title: Residency Match

numinance.kinds.v1.ResidencyPolicy.jsons.description:
ResidencyPolicy says where execution and inference may happen: the class derived from the executor's live
 configuration must meet every floor that applies, or the Change is refused at start (ADR 0019).

extensions.description: extensions holds vendor or customer data under reverse-DNS keys; the Engine never reads it.

metadata.description: metadata is required; the loader enforces it, the schema cannot.

spec.description: spec is required; the loader enforces it, the schema cannot.

numinance.kinds.v1.ResidencyPolicy.jsons.title: Residency Policy

cross_region.description: cross_region is true when inference may run in a region other than the source region; absent means false.

floors.description:
floors are the residency floors; only an org-scoped kind or a control pack may set them. Absent in the org means
 the floor IN_ACCOUNT, which pack floors add to and never displace; an org lowers it only by writing one.

regions.description:
regions is required and non-empty: the allowed source and destination regions, each one region name ("*" is
 refused). A list cannot carry FORBID, so the profile context refuses it below the org scope until tighten-only.

require_customer_keying.description: require_customer_keying is true when data at rest must be encrypted with customer-managed keys; absent means false.

retention_max.description: retention_max is the longest a model vendor may retain prompts and responses; absent means no retention.

training_use.description:
training_use says whether a model vendor may train on prompts and responses (ADR 0019). Absent means TRAINING_USE_FORBIDDEN; it is optional so that no document that omits it changes meaning. Setting TRAINING_USE_ALLOWED
 widens what is permitted, so like the other limits it carries FORBID and only the org sets it.
training_use.title: Training Use

numinance.kinds.v1.ResidencyPolicySpec.j.title: Residency Policy Spec

numinance.kinds.v1.ResidencyRule.jsonsch.description: ResidencyRule adds a floor for the changes it matches.

match.description: match is required; the loader enforces it, the schema cannot.

numinance.kinds.v1.ResidencyRule.jsonsch.title: Residency Rule
